title: microqueue pacing field notes
content:
Context and goal:
Quick playbook-style notes from trying a microqueue-based pacing layer to smooth tiny ingress bursts. Objective was not to find the one true configuration but to capture surprising behaviors and quick mitigations to feed into the A/B rollout.

Test harness summary:
- Runner: local kube cluster (3x g4dn.12xlarge emulated), runtime build: canary-2024-10-28
- Model: open-llama-7b (int8 quant build + experimental 4-bit fallback path enabled)
- Sequence lengths: 32 tokens typical, 128 for stress samples
- Workload generator: custom Poisson+burst generator (made small bursts at 0.5s intervals), seeds logged
- Concurrency per pod: 16 slots, per-slot batch cap = 8 tokens
- KV cache behavior: warm-warm (primed), cold-warm (cold KV for first 15s of run)

Important commands used (for reproducibility):
- start runner: ./run_bench --nodes=3 --concurrency=16 --burst=on --pacer=microqueue
- capture tracing: curl http://localhost:21000/trace/start?run=nov2

Experiments and observations (ordered rough chronology):
1) baseline (no microqueue):
  - p50: 28ms, p95: 72ms, p99: 210ms, qps sustained: 180 (32-token inputs)
  - notes: clear saw-tooth in request qps; tail spikes aligned with scheduler wakeups.

2) naive microqueue enabled (single global queue, 10ms dispatch window):
  - p50: 32ms (+4ms), p95: 85ms (+13ms), p99: 240ms (+30ms), qps: 185 (+5)
  - notes: average latency rose slightly but steady-state QPS increased small; p99 worse due to microbatch queueing long tail when single slow request blocks window.

3) microqueue + per-priority lanes (foreground/background), window 8ms foreground, 20ms background:
  - p50: 30ms, p95: 78ms, p99: 170ms, qps: 190
  - notes: moving foreground to tighter lane reduced p99 substantially. Background lane absorbing heavy requests reduces head-of-line blocking.

4) microqueue + adaptive slot cap (decrease window if backlog > 12, increase if idle):
  - p50: 29ms, p95: 74ms, p99: 150ms, qps: 198
  - notes: adaptive strategy improved throughput and lowered tail. But saw oscillation when adaptive hysteresis thresholds too tight (5s).

5) cold-KV priming path (simulated new key eviction every 30s):
  - when cold requests hit: p99 leaps to 480ms in baseline; with microqueue+foreground lane: p99 spikes to 380ms but recovers faster (under 3 windows)
  - observation: microqueue reduces the frequency of large tail events by spreading cold-KV cost across small windows, but doesn't eliminate them. Consider explicit cold-KV admission gating.

6) quantization impact (4-bit path engaged on half of pods as fallback):
  - 4-bit pods: individual p50 22ms lower but variance higher when mixed fleet used (due to heterogeneous processing times)
  - mixed fleet + microqueue: p95 became bimodal; microqueue sometimes groups fast 4-bit + slow int8 which increased p99.
  - mitigation: add affinity/pod-tag-based routing into lanes so similar-latency pods batched together.

Surprising behaviors and short notes:
- tiny burst of 6 concurrent requests with 8ms dispatch window created a micro-saturation that amplified kernel scheduling jitter; this showed as 40–60ms spikes in p99 when minibatches pushed GPU context-switching.
- proactive padding (inserting 1–2ms jitter/random delay) occasionally reduces pathological alignment of expensive ops — ugly, but effective as a short-term mitigation.
- observed one case where an early batching decision deferred a request for ~120ms because of scheduler race between queue-drainer and autoscaler probe. Need stronger ordering guarantees between drainer and probe thread.

Quick numerical summary (representative run with adaptive lanes + affinity):
- steady qps: 205
- p50: 27ms
- p95: 69ms
- p99: 140ms
- cold-KV p99 (first 20s of run): 360ms

Next action items (short):
- Short term (this sprint):
  1) implement lane-level pod affinity tag so microqueue batches only same-latency pods (PR: GHPR #2048).
  2) add cold-KV gate: mark requests with KV miss and route to background lane with prefetch token.
  3) tune adaptive hysteresis to 10s low, 30s high to avoid oscillation.

- Investigation tickets:
  - INF-6732: quantify alignment jitter across different container runtimes (runc vs kata)
  - bench: run mixed-quant fleet with pod-affinity and capture batch composition histograms

Notes to self (loose):
- keep a small script that replays the exact RNG seed (generator logs directory).
- record per-batch composition (latency, pods involved) for next run; need a small tracer hook in batching path.

Conclusions (one-paragraph):
Microqueue-style pacing can meaningfully increase steady-state throughput and lower median latency if coupled with priority lanes and adaptive windowing, but it also makes heterogeneous fleets and cold-KV paths more visible at the tail. Short-term mitigations (lane affinity, cold-KV gating) are straightforward and should be validated before any wider rollout.

Raw artifacts referenced (local):
- /tmp/bench/nov2/run-2024-11-02-trace.log
- /tmp/bench/nov2/batch-composition.csv

If anyone wants to re-run or dig in ping me (Aarav) on slack and I can share the harness and seeds.
